{

  "title": "Slab Thickness Alarm and Fault History",
  "difficulty": "medium",
  "requirements": "# Slab Thickness Alarm and Fault History\n\n- **Difficulty:** Medium (medium)\n\n## Requirements\n\nMonitor slab-thickness faults on a stone-cutting line, including minimum alarm holding, fault counting, normal-cutting runtime accumulation and a history of the five most recent faults.\n\n1. When THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID is TRUE, THICKNESS_FAULT indicates that thickness deviation exceeds tolerance. Activate THICKNESS_ALARM immediately when the fault becomes TRUE, and hold each triggered alarm for at least 500 ms. Keep the alarm active while the fault persists.\n2. On each FALSE-to-TRUE transition of a valid fault signal, increment Slab_Fault_Counter and store the current FaultTimestamp in element 0 of Slab_Fault_History. Shift older entries toward higher indices, retaining only the five most recent entries.\n3. Accumulate Slab_Runtime_Accumulator using CycleTime only while CUTTING_RUN is TRUE, the thickness signal is valid and no thickness fault is present. Otherwise preserve the accumulated value.\n4. At power-up or whenever THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID is FALSE, switch off the alarm and clear its holding state. Do not add fault records or accumulate normal runtime while the signal is invalid.\n5. At power-up, initialize the fault count, accumulated runtime and all five history entries to zero. Statistics and history are for observation and maintenance only; they must not alter the cutting equipment's operating permissive, and external callers must not modify history entries.\n\n## Interface Definition\n\n| Direction | Variable/Field | Data Type | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Input | `THICKNESS_FAULT` | `BOOL` | Thickness deviation exceeds the permitted tolerance. |\n| Input | `THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID` | `BOOL` | Thickness-signal validity; FALSE means the signal is lost or unavailable. |\n| Input | `CUTTING_RUN` | `BOOL` | Actual cutting-equipment running status. |\n| Input | `FaultTimestamp` | `DINT` | Current timestamp in seconds, used as the fault-record identifier. |\n| Input | `CycleTime` | `TIME` | Actual elapsed interval represented by this invocation; must be positive. |\n| Output | `THICKNESS_ALARM` | `BOOL` | Thickness alarm with a minimum 500 ms hold duration. |\n| Output | `Slab_Fault_Counter` | `UINT` | Number of valid thickness-fault occurrences. |\n| Output | `Slab_Runtime_Accumulator` | `LTIME` | Accumulated normal-cutting runtime. |\n| Output | `Slab_Fault_History` | `ARRAY[0..4] OF DINT` | Five most recent fault timestamps; index 0 is newest; read-only to callers. |",
  "scenario": "Thickness monitoring records faults, alarm minimum holding, normal-cutting time and bounded history.",

A transition affects the same observed scan. dt_ms is elapsed time since the preceding invocation; the first invocation starts IEC timers at elapsed zero. CycleTime inputs, where supplied, are attributed to the current invocation rather than inferred from dt_ms.",

    "Slab_Fault_Counter": "O[k].Slab_Fault_Counter: independently observed post-scan candidate value (UINT); never defined as expected output.",
    "Slab_Runtime_Accumulator": "O[k].Slab_Runtime_Accumulator: independently observed post-scan candidate value (LTIME); never defined as expected output.",
    "Slab_Fault_History": "O[k].Slab_Fault_History: independently observed post-scan candidate value (ARRAY[0..4] OF DINT); never defined as expected output.",

      "encoding_status": "NOT_LOWERED_TO_MODEL_CHECKER",
      "scope": "INITIAL_INSTANCE"
    },

      "id": "PUB012.P1",
      "name": "Signal loss",
      "formula": "G(!valid -> !alarm)",
      "explanation": "Invalid signal cancels alarm immediately.",
      "language": "LTL_OVER_TYPED_SCAN_PREDICATES",
      "encoding_status": "NOT_LOWERED_TO_MODEL_CHECKER",
      "scope": "SCAN_SEQUENCE"
    },

      "encoding_status": "NOT_LOWERED_TO_MODEL_CHECKER",
      "scope": "SCAN_SEQUENCE"
    },
    {
      "id": "PUB012.P3",
      "name": "Occurrence",

      "explanation": "Each valid rising fault shifts the bounded history.",
      "language": "LTL_OVER_TYPED_SCAN_PREDICATES",
